overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 17
overview.text: In this lesson, you will discover the power of factoring to solve higher-degree equations. The Zero-Product Property guarantees that if the product of multiple factors equals zero, at least one of the factors must be zero. This converts a quadratic equation into two simple linear equations.
outcomes: Understand and apply the Zero-Product Property: $ab = 0 \iff a = 0 \text{ or } b = 0$.
Solve quadratic equations written in factored form $(x - p)(x - q) = 0$.
Factor out common monomial factors to solve equations like $3x^2 + 27x = 0$.
overview.teacherInsight: Caution students that the Zero-Product Property ONLY works when the expression is set equal to ZERO. If $(x - 2)(x - 3) = 6$, you CANNOT conclude $x - 2 = 6$ or $x - 3 = 1$; you must first expand, subtract 6 to get standard form $x^2 - 5x = 0$, and refactor.

content.html:
Interactive Zero-Product Property Solver

Adjust roots $p$ and $q$ for $(x - p)(x - q) = 0$. Observe how each factor produces an independent linear equation.

Root 1 ($p$):p = 3
Root 2 ($q$):q = -2
(x - 3)(x + 2) = 0
Factor 1: x - 3 = 0 ⇒ x = 3
Factor 2: x + 2 = 0 ⇒ x = -2
Solution Set: {-2, 3}

vocabulary.definition: If the product of two real numbers is zero, then at least one of the numbers must be zero: ab = 0 implies a = 0 or b = 0.
An expression expressed as a product of irreducible linear or polynomial factors.
The input values that cause an expression or function to evaluate to zero.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the solution set to $3x^2 + 27x = 0$?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Factor out greatest common factor $3x$: $3x(x + 9) = 0$. By Zero-Product Property, $3x = 0 \implies x = 0$ or $x + 9 = 0 \implies x = -9$. Solution set is $\{0, -9\}$.

practiceQuestions.question: Why can the Zero-Product Property NOT be applied directly to $(x - 1)(x - 2) = 12$?
options: Because the right-hand side is 12, not 0. Factors can multiply to 12 in infinite real combinations without either factor being 12.
Because the equation has negative numbers.
Because quadratic equations can never equal 12.
The property can be applied directly, yielding $x = 13$.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Zero-Product Property is unique to 0. If $ab = 12$, $a$ and $b$ could be 3 and 4, 2 and 6, etc. You must expand to $x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0$ and refactor to $(x - 5)(x + 2) = 0$.
